prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_F:
Labour Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core approach
- Budget Responsibility Lock: cut the deficit every year; get debt falling and a current budget surplus ASAP; no new spending paid for by extra borrowing; OBR to audit party manifestos.

Tax and public finances
- Restore 50p top rate over £150k; introduce a 10p starting rate funded by ending the Marriage Allowance.
- No rises in basic/higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; no VAT extension to essentials.
- Abolish non-dom status; clamp down on avoidance/evasion; review HMRC culture.

Economy, industry and infrastructure
- National Infrastructure Commission; support HS2 and northern rail, strategic roads, cycling; swift airport-capacity decision.
- Long-term science funding; leadership in low-carbon tech; decarbonise power by 2030; empower Green Investment Bank; create an Energy Security Board.
- British Investment Bank and regional banks; boost high-street banking competition; payday lender levy.
- Support small firms: cut then freeze business rates; tackle late payment.
- Digital: universal affordable high-speed broadband and wider mobile coverage.
- Corporate governance reforms: empower long-term investors; curb short-termism; employee voice on pay.
- Royal Mail: retain 30% public stake; staff-led trust for employee shares.

Work, pay and opportunities
- Raise National Minimum Wage to >£8/hour by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage via procurement and “Make Work Pay” tax rebates.
- Ban exploitative zero-hours contracts; close agency-worker loopholes; scrap employment tribunal fees system.
- Youth/jobs: compulsory Jobs Guarantee (bank bonus tax-funded); guarantee an apprenticeship for qualified school leavers; expand public-sector apprenticeships; create Technical Degrees; reduce tuition fees to £6,000; Youth Allowance tied to training; curb unpaid internships.

Consumer markets and transport
- Freeze energy bills until 2017; reform market (separate generation/supply, open exchange, tougher watchdog); 1m interest-free efficiency loans; PRS minimum energy standards.
- Water affordability scheme; stronger regulation.
- Rail reform: allow a public operator; fare freeze for a year then caps; legal right to cheapest ticket; devolve bus powers and integrate local transport.

NHS and care
- Fund 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives (mansion tax, tobacco levy, anti-avoidance).
- 48-hour GP appointments; one-week cancer tests and a Cancer Treatments Fund.
- Repeal Health and Social Care Act; NHS preferred provider; cap private profits; integrate physical, mental and social care; mental health parity with 28-day access to talking therapies.
- Public health: limits on sugar/salt/fat in foods marketed to children.
- End 15-minute care visits; recruit 5,000 home-care workers; stronger support for carers.

Education and children
- Protect entire education budget (early years to post-16).
- Technical Baccalaureate; Institutes of Technical Education; English/Maths to 18; independent careers advice.
- All teachers qualified; Master Teacher status; School Leadership Institute.
- Local Directors of School Standards; end Free Schools programme; cap infant classes at 30; require private-school partnerships with state schools.
- Compulsory, age-appropriate sex and relationships education; character and anti-bullying programmes.

Families, housing and welfare
- Free childcare 25 hours for 3–4s (working parents); wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave to 4 weeks and raise pay.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first dibs for local first-time buyers; “use it or lose it” on land; garden cities; back small builders and public building.
- Private renting: three-year tenancies as standard; ceiling on excessive rent rises; ban letting fees; landlord register.
- Abolish the Bedroom Tax; keep household benefit cap (review locally); tailored back-to-work support; pause/review Universal Credit; reform Work Capability Assessment; specialist disability employment support; protect pension triple lock; restrict Winter Fuel Payments for richest 5%.

Immigration, policing and justice
- 1,000 extra border staff; exit checks; tighter short-term study visas; retain non-EU worker cap; two-year wait for benefits; English requirement for public-facing roles.
- Ban undercutting by agencies; extend Gangmasters Authority remit; humane asylum (end indefinite detention for vulnerable groups).
- Safeguard 10,000 police officers by abolishing PCCs, sharing services; Local Policing Commitment; replace IPCC; Victims’ Law; tougher action on domestic abuse; ban “legal highs”.
- Stronger counter-extremism (controls on dangerous suspects, revamped Prevent, de-radicalisation for returnees); zero-tolerance of hate crime.

Devolution, rights and media
- Constitutional Convention; replace House of Lords with an elected Senate of the Nations and Regions.
- English Devolution Act: £30bn to city/county regions; integrate local transport; retain growth business rates; local Public Accounts Committees.
- Implement further powers for Scotland and Wales; fair funding for Wales; support NI progress.
- Votes at 16; fix voter registration; cap party donations; statutory lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships/consultancies.
- Protect Human Rights Act; extend FOI to major private providers of public services; gender pay-gap reporting; race equality strategy; strengthen LGBT rights; media plurality; implement Leveson; keep BBC strong and Channel 4 public.

Europe, defence, climate and development
- Remain in and reform the EU (single market completion, budget discipline, worker rights); “referendum lock” on any power transfers.
- NATO commitment; cautious, legal, multilateral approach to interventions; two-state solution for Israel/Palestine.
- Strategic Defence and Security Review; strengthen Armed Forces Covenant; Veterans’ Register; bolster cyber security; maintain independent nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Lead on climate: push for Paris deal, net zero global emissions in the second half of the century.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; focus on poorest, women and children; create Centre for Universal Health Coverage; strengthen tax transparency and anti-corruption.

TEXT_E:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision: Secure a strong economy to fund public services and improve life “at every stage,” rewarding work, spreading opportunity, and keeping Britain safe.

Economy and tax
- Eliminate the deficit, run a surplus from 2018–19, and keep debt falling; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Raise Personal Allowance to £12,500 and higher-rate threshold to £50,000; new “Tax-Free Minimum Wage” link so 30 hours on the Minimum Wage pays no Income Tax.
- Crack down on tax evasion/avoidance; keep competitive business taxes and simplify the system.

Jobs and business
- Create 2 million more jobs and achieve full employment; support small firms via business rates review, red tape cuts, prompt payment, Start Up Loans, and export support.
- Deliver 3 million new apprenticeships; abolish employers’ NICs for apprentices under 25; tackle long‑term youth unemployment with a time‑limited Youth Allowance and “earn or learn” requirements.

Infrastructure and regional growth
- Over £100bn infrastructure investment: HS2/HS3, rail electrification, Crossrail, £15bn for roads, cycling and ultra‑low emission vehicles.
- Universal superfast broadband to 95% by end‑2017; improve mobile coverage and lead on 5G.
- Build a “Northern Powerhouse” and devolve powers/budgets to cities with elected mayors.

Housing
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy and introduce Help to Buy ISA.
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under‑40s), 275,000 additional affordable homes; extend Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants; prioritize brownfield and protect the Green Belt.

Welfare and childcare
- Reduce household benefit cap to £23,000; freeze working‑age benefits for two years (key exemptions); roll out Universal Credit.
- 30 hours’ free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; tax‑free childcare up to £2,000 per child.

NHS and social care
- Increase NHS spending every year; at least £8bn extra by 2020 to deliver a 7‑day NHS and same‑day GP access for over‑75s.
- Integrate health and social care (Better Care Fund); focus on mental health, cancer, dementia; expand digital access and transparency.

Education and skills
- Protect per‑pupil funding; zero tolerance of failing/coasting schools; expand academies and free schools (500 new).
- Tougher standards in literacy/numeracy; core academic GCSEs; 17,500 extra maths/physics teachers; no cap on university places; new postgraduate loans; expand technical routes (UTCs, Degree Apprenticeships).

Immigration
- Target net migration in the tens of thousands.
- EU reforms: four‑year residency before in‑work benefits/social housing; end child benefit for children abroad; tougher deportation and re‑entry rules; stronger enforcement and action on illegal working.

Law, security and rights
- Complete police reform; modernize prisons; new Victims’ Law; tougher sentences for serious crime.
- Counter‑extremism powers (banning/extremism disruption orders); update communications data laws.
- Replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills down via competition and smart meters; support shale with community benefits; back nuclear and value‑for‑money renewables; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give locals final say.
- Meet climate commitments cost‑effectively; protect nature with a “Blue Belt,” plant 11m trees, improve air/water, expand flood defences.

Pensions and older people
- Keep triple lock; introduce single‑tier pension; protect pensioner benefits; cap residential care costs; raise effective Inheritance Tax threshold on the family home to £1m for couples.

Constitution, EU and foreign policy
- English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland and Wales; support NI settlement.
- Hold an in/out EU referendum by end‑2017; reform EU, protect Single Market, keep the pound.
- Maintain strong Armed Forces (retain Trident), meet NATO commitments, and spend 0.7% GNI on international development.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_E aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

}
